binding_record_note: Two protected lookup overloads, hashCode and isEqual for each ordered family, each bound once to its real compiler-emitted Rust body. These scoped partial records grant no global API or original-test mapping credit.
changes: Added lookup_node, lookup_node_with_hash, bounded_hash and keys_equal to both ordered containers through one shared bridge macro. Methods retain only the native HashPolicy key bound, without Debug, Clone or Default requirements on payloads or policies.

Lookup writes typed actual-node pointers directly into the caller output. Empty lookup preserves the preexisting node pointer; the hash-output overload still evaluates the hash before its empty check.

A hash callback failure leaves both original outputs unchanged. An equality callback failure leaves the node output at the current bucket-chain candidate, and preserves the already-produced bounded hash where applicable.

Successful lookup preserves native bucket-chain traversal and predicate argument order; a miss writes null only after exhausting candidates. Existing map lookup now uses the same traversal rather than maintaining a second implementation.

bounded_hash preserves one-based native modulo arithmetic for positive upper bounds; direct native samples include zero/one/full-width hash values and one/thirteen/full-width moduli. keys_equal invokes the policy once with unchanged argument order.

Direct native oracle tests cover nineteen lookup states/failure prefixes per family, including collision-chain head/middle/tail hits and misses, nine hash-bound combinations per family, and equality success/false/throw cases.

Pointer outputs refer to existing nodes without allocating, cloning, rehashing or changing cursor registry state. Strict Miri checks include dereferencing the returned live node identity after callback failure.
The implementation is based on current main independently of the pending ordered constructor-lifetime candidate and does not edit allocator or shared BaseMap code.
limitations: This is a bounded class-by-class protected-method slice; class-wide and global API/test parity remain incomplete.
Returned raw pointers grant no new safe mutable access or lifetime extension. Callers must obey the map node lifetime, mutation, ownership and aliasing requirements before dereferencing a pointer.
The native zero-upper-bound remainder is undefined. Rust explicitly panics before a hash callback when upper is zero; native oracle comparisons cover only the defined positive-modulus domain.

Native subclass layout and C++ protected access control are represented by explicit Rust methods rather than inheritance. Protected appendToList, unlinkFromList and generic forwarding helper surfaces remain separate work.
Arbitrary foreign bucket-node injection or invariant-breaking raw writes are not certified. Traversal assumes the canonical graph is valid and its typed nodes remain live.
Existing safe detached cursor owner validation, non-owning registry overhead and safe set FirstNode unit views remain separate representation/API adaptations.
Pending constructor/failure-lifetime work is not included in this independent base; prior receipts remain immutable. This slice makes no new default/copy/move constructor or allocator-handle claims.
Scoped native/compiler/Miri evidence does not replace whole-workspace validation or global completeness proof.
compiler_warning_note: Nightly rustdoc warnings outside this lookup scope are retained in raw output; scoped Clippy is run with warnings denied.
